one_liner: Header-only x86 C library: SIMD popcount, positional popcount and AND/OR/XOR bitmap cardinalities, with CPUID dispatch.
what_it_does: One header, libalgebra.h, offers STORM_popcnt(data, bytes), STORM_pospopcnt_u16(data, n_values, out[16]), and STORM_intersect_count / STORM_union_count / STORM_diff_count(a, b, n_words) for the AND, OR and XOR cardinalities of two 64-bit-word bitmaps. Getters (STORM_get_intersect_count_func and friends) return the best kernel for a given length. These are plain C functions over raw arrays, not a container type, and they replace a hand-written popcount loop rather than any std:: API. The header bundles kernels from libpopcnt, positional-popcount and CRoaring (their licences are embedded).
how_it_is_fast: It runs the Harley-Seal carry-save-adder popcount from Lemire, Kurz and Mula (2016) with SSE4.2, AVX2 and AVX-512BW. AVX-512 uses vpternlogd for the adder, and AVX2 inputs shorter than 64 words use Mula's pshufb nibble-lookup kernel. Positional popcount uses the Klarqvist/Mula/Lemire blend-popcnt, adder-forest and Harley-Seal kernels. CPUID and XGETBV are read once at run time and the kernel is picked by length, so you need no -march flags.
when_to_use: Counting set bits, or AND/OR/XOR cardinalities, of large bitmaps (hundreds to millions of 64-bit words) on x86-64 with AVX2 or AVX-512BW. The README shows popcount 12-21x over a byte-lookup loop between 512 and 16384 words, falling to about 3-4x once data leaves cache.
Similarity or overlap scores between dense bitsets (Jaccard or Hamming counts from intersect/union/diff) where you only need the count, not the result bitmap.
Per-bit-position counts over uint16 flag arrays (for example SAM/BAM FLAG statistics) via STORM_pospopcnt_u16.
A portable binary built without -march that should still use AVX2/AVX-512 where available, thanks to the target attributes and run-time dispatch.
when_not_to_use: Whenever exact counts matter on arbitrary lengths without your own tests: by reading the code, STORM_popcnt returns wrong counts for many lengths that are not powers of two (see gotchas). Modelling its index arithmetic in Python gave wrong results for 253 of 513 eight-byte-multiple sizes from 0 to 4096 bytes on an AVX-512BW CPU and 450 of 513 on an SSE4.2-only CPU.

ARM/aarch64: despite the README's NEON claim, the header has no NEON code and includes <x86intrin.h> unconditionally for every non-MSVC compiler, so it does not compile there. Use libpopcnt or std::popcount instead.

MSVC builds that want SIMD: the SSE/AVX2 kernels are compiled only under /arch:AVX2, where the STORM_TARGET macro expands to a stray `0` before each function (not compiled here). AppVeyor CI builds without /arch, so only the scalar POPCNT path is ever tested on Windows.
Tiny inputs (under about 32 words): the README shows 0.8-1.4x, so there is nothing to gain.
If you need a maintained dependency: last commit 2019-12-16, no releases, issues #1 and #5 (int loop counters against size_t lengths) still open.

integration.dependencies: none (benchmark.cpp needs Linux perf_event for -p mode)
integration.min_toolchain: SIMD kernels need GCC 4.9+ (AVX-512BW GCC 5+) or Clang 3.8+; benchmark built with -std=c++11; C11 or C++ for the dispatch
integration.platforms: x86 / x86-64 only in practice (SSE4.2, AVX2, AVX-512BW chosen at run time); no NEON code despite the README
integration.thread_safety: not documented; dispatch caches CPUID in a function-local static (C++11 magic static, or a __sync CAS in C) and the kernels are pure functions of read-only input, so concurrent calls look safe
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — no std:: equivalent; it replaces a hand-written popcount or AND+popcount loop, with byte lengths for STORM_popcnt, 16-bit-value counts for pospopcnt and 64-bit-word counts for set algebra

gotchas: Correctness bugs in STORM_popcnt's remainder handling (found by reading libalgebra.h at the 2019-12-16 head; not compiled, since the enrichment rules forbid building). (1) STORM_popcnt_csa_sse4 and the SSE intersect/union/diff CSA kernels end with `cnt64 = STORM_POPCOUNT_SSE(...)` instead of `+=`, so whenever the 128-bit vector count is not a multiple of 16 they return only the last vector's popcount; this path serves 256-511 byte inputs on every SSE4.2+ CPU. (2) STORM_popcnt_avx2 points its SSE tail at &data[n_cycles_sse*4] instead of &data[n_cycles*4], so it double-counts words 4-5 and drops the last two words when n_words % 4 is 2 or 3 (512-1023 bytes on AVX-512 CPUs, all sizes from 512 bytes on AVX2 CPUs). (3) STORM_popcnt_avx512 starts its scalar tail at 8*n_cycles + 4*n_cycles instead of 4*n_cycles_avx2, so it drops the last word of any odd-word input of 1024 bytes or more. Example from the model: 272 bytes gives 67 instead of 1100 on AVX-512BW. On AVX2/AVX-512 machines the set-algebra kernels are correct; on SSE4.2-only CPUs intersect/union/diff are wrong for 1890 of 2017 lengths from 32 to 2048 words.

The benchmark cannot catch these bugs: every tested size is a power of two (4 to 1048576 words), the popcount cross-check `assert(a == b)` is removed by the Release build's -DNDEBUG, and the set-algebra path has no check at all. The published speedups therefore come only from the bug-free power-of-two paths.

The README overstates and misdocuments the API: it names STORM_get_intersection_count_func, but the header defines STORM_get_intersect_count_func. It says pospopcnt's size is in bytes, but the code loops over len uint16 values, so passing a byte count reads twice past the buffer. The pospopcnt speedup table is copied from mklarqvist/positional-popcount, and benchmark.cpp never runs pospopcnt.

Harness details: cycles are user-space perf counters, minimum of 10000 single calls, with freshly generated (cache-hot) data before each call; at 4-32 words the ioctl fringe dominates. LinuxEvents never sizes its `ids` vector before ioctl(PERF_EVENT_IOC_ID, &ids[i]) (undefined behaviour; the return is unchecked) and closes only the last of six perf fds per call (about 760 leaked over a full run). The scalar set-algebra fallback uses inline-asm popcnt without a CPUID check.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Use it only for its one-header bundle of popcount plus AND/OR/XOR cardinalities with run-time dispatch, and only on power-of-two or self-tested lengths. Otherwise prefer the catalogued sources it repackages: libpopcnt for plain popcount, positional-popcount (same author, where the pospopcnt numbers come from) for positional counts, CRoaring for compressed bitmap set algebra, and sse-popcount as the reference kernels. sse-popcount's catalogued run puts AVX-512 Harley-Seal at about 3.6x over a 64-bit POPCNT loop, a fairer yardstick than libalgebra's byte-lookup baseline.
verified_claims_summary: On a Cannon Lake Core i3-8121U with gcc 8.2.1 (CMake Release, -O3 -DNDEBUG, -std=c++11, kernels picked by CPUID), minimum user-space cycles per 64-bit word over 10000 runs. The dispatched popcount was 16.4x faster than an 8-bit-lookup scalar loop with vectorization disabled at 1024 words, 21x at 8192 and 4.2x at 1048576; AND/OR/XOR cardinality was 15.3x faster at 1024 word pairs and 2.8x at 1048576 (0.8x at 4). Against a hardware POPCNT loop the gain would be much smaller (catalogued libpopcnt and sse-popcount tables suggest roughly 2-4x; not measured here).
status_note: Abandoned since 2019-12-16 (45 stars, no releases) and Apache-2.0, so it is easy to vendor as one header, but fix the three remainder bugs (cnt64 = vs +=, the AVX2 SSE-tail pointer, the AVX-512 tail index) and test non-power-of-two lengths before trusting its counts.
